outcome.shown: A bicycle stays upright primarily through a combination of rider input and self-stabilizing mechanical design. While the gyroscopic effect of the spinning wheels provides some stability at higher speeds, the most critical factor is the bike's steering geometry—specifically the "trail," which causes the front wheel to naturally steer into the direction of a lean, effectively positioning the wheels back under the center of mass to correct the balance. This mechanical self-correction is supplemented by the rider, who makes constant, intuitive micro-adjustments to the handlebars and shifts their body weight to maintain equilibrium, allowing the bicycle to remain stable even at relatively low speeds.
